source_reviews.independent_solution:
**317.** Draw each subgroup on common axes as full lines.
a: (k,l)=(2,0),(2,-3),(2,4). Construction pairs:
[(0,0),(1,2)], [(0,-3),(1,-1)], [(0,4),(1,6)].
They are distinct parallel rising lines; y=2x+4 is above y=2x,
which is above y=2x-3 at every same x.
b: (k,l)=(-0.5,0),(-0.5,-2),(-0.5,3). Construction pairs:
[(0,0),(2,-1)], [(0,-2),(2,-3)], [(0,3),(2,2)].
They are distinct parallel falling lines, ordered +3,0,-2 from top to bottom.
If all six are on one system, lines from different subgroups intersect;
only lines within each subgroup are parallel.

source_reviews.independent_solution:
**325. Source precision issue.** Plot all ten observed (V,m) pairs, with
horizontal V in litres and vertical m in kilograms. They form an approximately
straight rising scatter, but not an exact straight line: the first two
successive slopes are (1.54-1.12)/0.5=0.84 kg/L and
(1.91-1.54)/0.5=0.74 kg/L. Thus no affine function matches all entries exactly.
A concrete approximate graphical model is m approximately 0.8V+0.72;
every displayed measurement is within 0.02 kg of it. Under that explicitly
approximate model, empty-can mass is about 0.72 kg and 1 litre of kerosene
has mass about 0.8 kg (slope), not the total can-plus-liquid mass at V=1.
The source supplies no measurement tolerance or fitting convention. Exact
linearity and unique exact values for these parameters are unsupported;
that exact claim is unresolved, not silently accepted. A rough graphical
estimate is possible only with its approximation stated.

as distinct elements. The equality relation is exactly
R={(0.05,1/20),(0.2,1/5),(0.25,1/4)}, three distinct ordered pairs.
Listing the source's fraction spellings gives four representation matches:
(0.05,1/20),(0.2,3/15),(0.2,9/45),(0.25,7/28), but the middle two denote
the SAME mathematical pair. Also 0.3!=1/3, so 0.3 has no partner.
The relation is determined; only a representation-based count would need
wording that distinguishes written fraction labels from numerical set members.
